answer: Each agent drops one anchor: a public key-signed log naming one berth. Two logs, one key, two berths prove equivocation, dropping that identity to its nadir: its 70-credit bond burns, half to the prover. Fake log k costs 70+6(k-1), so 1,000 fakes pay 3,067,000 against a 40,000 pool. Rented logs fail: one log worn by two keys is itself a contradiction. Honest agents file one true log, pay 70 once, and take their full share of the nectar.
